target_customer: Business teams, freelancers and agencies that want to build web apps without code, and IT leaders who need them governed
problem: Building web frontends and apps normally needs engineers. No-code tools were either too limited or locked users into one backend.
business_model: SaaS subscription tiers for the visual builder, plus a marketplace and academy
product_category: No-code frontend and full-stack app builder

founders.name: Raphael Goldsztejn
education: Neoma Business School (graduate, per YC page)
founders.background_notes: YC page describes him as a hands-on builder with 10+ years of product and engineering experience.

founders.name: Florian Briou
founders.background_notes: No bio on YC page or company about page.

founders.name: Marc Fabre
founders.background_notes: Titled CTO on the company about page. No bio found.

competitors.name: Webflow
competitors.what: Visual no-code website builder, the closest reference point for WeWeb's editor

competitors.name: Bubble
competitors.what: No-code full-stack web app builder with its own backend

technical_complexity.rationale: A visual editor that generates real Vue based frontends and connects to arbitrary backends (REST, Airtable, Xano) is hard engineering for a three person team.

defensibility.rationale: Apps built in the editor create some lock in, but several funded no-code builders offered similar editors.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source found of Webflow or Bubble copying the exact frontend only wedge; both expanded features over time. WeWeb remained independent.

market_need_then: No-code demand rose sharply in 2020 and 2021. The WeWeb about page says many early customers were already building web applications, not just sites, which pushed the 2022 move to WeWeb 2.0.

identity.logo: Wordmark with a playful logo; an agency case study describes a generative brand system
identity.mascot_or_character: A purple fox mascot adopted in 2021 per a community forum post
identity.visual_style: Playful, community focused identity per the agency case study
identity.voice_and_tone: Friendly and transparent; values include courage to be kind and transparent by default

branding.community_and_virality: Active community forum, a WeWeb Academy and a marketplace, and live chats with founders on the forum.

brand_strength.rationale: A mascot and an agency built identity plus an active forum show some brand work, but no press about the brand itself and the name is easy to confuse with generic web terms.

pivots.from: Website builder for small business owners
pivots.why: Per the company about page, customers were using it to build web applications.

outcome_analysis: WeWeb is still active with a small team. It rode the 2020 to 2021 no-code wave, raised a seed from French funds before and around YC, and moved from websites toward web apps in 2022 and AI assisted full stack building with version 3.0 in 2026. No acquisition, shutdown or layoff was found. Funding after the first round is not verified, so the scale of its capital is unknown.
notes: The round has no stated stage; the company about page says first round led by 42CAP and Aglae Ventures, and Nordic9 (dated 25 January 2020) gives a EUR 1M headline and USD 1.11M round value. Seedtable lists 1.24M total over 3 rounds; geo.sig.ai lists 3.24M and CB Insights 130K, all unverified and not recorded. Competitor sources are Product Hunt threads dated December 2021, about eleven months after the Winter 2021 batch start; traction and funding of those rivals not captured. The Product Hunt page links Webflow only through a user comment, so this is weak. The YC page lists founding year 2020 while one source says 2017 to 2019.
